comment: AL-77: the frame chain after the scene (src/terrain_core/enb.hpp, assets/shaders/terrain_core/enb*.hlsl): the scene in half floats, then AO + contact shadows, atmosphere (more height fog, the sun's in-scatter with phase g, aerial perspective towards aerial_tint, a sun halo), bloom, light shafts, the eye's adaptation, a tone curve (none | aces | agx) and the grade (lift/gamma/gain, contrast round pivot, saturation, vibrance, split toning by the time of day: day / golden / night tints, a vignette that may sink into umber, film grain) and warm point lights (the game's fires: strength, how much is left by day, their glow in the air). `preset` is the start; the game and the lab cycle the presets with U (the file is read again) or take --enb NAME; --no-enb (or a preset with "hdr": false) is the old 8-bit path with no chain at all. A preset may name a "base" preset it starts from; anything it does not say is neutral, so "classic" is the old picture.

enb.comment: Skyrim-with-ENB light in the project's dark 60s-fantasy key: deep but open shadows, warm amber light, cool blue-violet shade, haze that glows towards the sun, a soft painterly bloom, a little grain.

enb_soft.comment: The same light with less of the lens: no grain, a lighter vignette, AgX's gentler curve.

classic.comment: The picture before AL-77: nothing on, no tone curve (a clamp).
